title: Ferrari Enzo vs F50: The Real Difference
description:
The Ferrari Enzo and the Ferrari F50 are separated by seven years and one big idea. One is a six-litre machine with a paddle gearbox and active aerodynamics. The other is a four-point-seven litre car with a manual gearshift, no power steering and no anti-lock brakes. A magazine ranked the older one higher. This is the real difference, with every number sourced. Our sources are Wikipedia's pages on both cars, RM Sotheby's catalogue pages, Sports Car Market, Hagerty's valuation pages, the magazine evo, Jalopnik, the DuPont Registry and the Italian site Italpassion. They disagree on prices, dates and production counts, and we show each version. Our own arithmetic is labelled.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
